what_happened: On 2026-10-30 the the person running Athena re-asked async jobs A6-A9 and wrote "Depends on" in the middle of a sentence. The planner doesn't parse dependencies written that way, so it silently ignored the dependency and put A7 ahead of A6. The the person running Athena had already fixed the same mid-line dependency by hand in qzqk after fj7k. They did not check the other requests written the same way. They closed a934, hvm8 and tx89 and re-asked them as 8vyd, wz33 and 5kw1, with the dependency on its own line. No job record exists, so this is an intervention note.
cause: The planner accepts a request whose dependency is in a form it cannot parse, and it gives no warning. Whether a request's dependencies were read is visible only in the resulting order. The the person running Athena's fix for one request was manual and did not extend to its siblings, because nothing in Athena lists which dependencies were parsed or flags text that looks like a dependency but was not parsed.
prevention: At admission or planning, scan each request for dependency-like phrasing ("depends on", "after", "blocked by", or a job id near such words). If the phrasing is present but the parser found no dependency, refuse or warn loudly. Also print the parsed dependency list for each item when the plan is built, so an unparsed dependency shows up before any job runs. A cheaper alternative is to make the parser accept "Depends on" anywhere in the text.
proposed_request: Make the planner's dependency handling visible and safe. (1) When a queued request contains dependency-like wording such as "depends on", "after", or "blocked by" next to a job id or title, and the parser extracts no dependency from it, the plan must show a warning for that item, and admission must refuse it with a message that says to put the dependency on its own line. (2) The plan output must list the parsed dependencies for every item. (3) Add tests with three request shapes: a mid-sentence "Depends on X", a standalone-line "Depends on X", and a request with no dependency. Check that the first produces a warning or refusal, the second is parsed, and the third produces no warning. Run the new check against the existing queued requests and report which of them it would flag.
